newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks pay millions more into Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks pay millions more into Holocaust fund.

text.p: Swiss banks have pledged an extra 20 million Swiss francs ($13.7 million) for a Holocaust memorial fund launched by private-sector businesses as a gesture to victims of Nazi persecution, a bankers' group said on Tuesday.

The contribution tops up the fund, initiated last month with a 100 million franc donation from the three biggest banks, to 285 million francs. The Swiss National Bank has chipped in 100 million and Swiss industry another 65 million.

"On the basis on firm pledges, the Swiss Bankers' Association can state that more than 20 million francs in additional funds will shortly be paid into the special fund as a contribution from other banks," the banking industry group said.

"The banks hope that it will thus be possible to provide help quickly and in a targeted way to victims of the Holocaust/Shoa," it said in a statement. Shoa is the term used by some Jewish groups for the Holocaust.
International pressure and threats of boycotts galvanised big Swiss banks to start the fund, which is being coordinated by the Swiss government in Berne and world Jewish groups.
Each party to the fund has had different grounds for paying.
The commercial banks were trying to dispel accusations that they hoarded accounts left by Holocaust victims. The central bank was making amends for buying looted Nazi gold during World War Two.
Swiss machine makers and engineering industries have spoken of donating to the fund to help repair the tarnished image of Swiss business.

Some Swiss industrialists have been accused of helping the German war effort and profiting from Nazi crimes by using forced labour at plants in Germany or buying businesses cheaply after they were confiscated from Jewish owners.

The memorial fund is separate from the seven billion franc Swiss Solidarity Foundation proposed by Berne that would sell official gold reserves to finance aid for victims of poverty, catastrophes and human rights abuses, including the Holocaust.
